role_title: OTC Alpha Product, 6 Months Full-time Internship (Jul-Dec 2026)
archetype_reasoning: The role centers on managing delivery pipelines, Jira workflows, and cross-functional reporting for an enterprise OTC derivatives product team — execution-heavy platform PM work inside a regulated financial services environment.
top_signals: delivery pipeline management and cross-functional execution tracking
Jira and structured workflow tooling to drive backlog hygiene and accountability
reporting and transparency — dashboards, risk flags, and leadership read-outs
hook_angle: A moment where Akshat discovered that execution opacity — not technical complexity — was the real blocker to enterprise trust: at Hevo, the inability to audit batch job status was killing deals, not the feature gaps themselves.
story_reasoning: Job Monitoring is the sharpest match — Akshat built an audit and visibility surface that directly reduced MTTR and drove trial-to-close, which mirrors this role's focus on transparency, delivery tracking, and accountability; Intuit Incident adds cross-functional coordination under pressure as a secondary signal.
company_research_angle: State Street's OTC Alpha platform is part of its broader push to modernize post-trade processing for institutional clients — the tension worth referencing is how legacy custodian-bank delivery models (manual, siloed, compliance-first) are being retooled for real-time trade lifecycle management, and how product and ops teams must create visibility layers that satisfy both front-office speed expectations and back-office regulatory requirements.
tone_reasoning: State Street is a 200-year-old custodian bank operating in a regulated, institutional capital markets environment — the letter must signal maturity, precision, and professional seriousness rather than startup energy.
gaps: No direct experience with OTC derivatives, capital markets instruments, or post-trade processing
No explicit Jira-as-primary-tool experience surfaced in portfolio stories (though engineering background implies familiarity)
No prior work inside a regulated financial services or custodian-bank environment
first_90_day_bet: Map every open Jira epic on the OTC Alpha board to its stated acceptance criteria and delivery owner, surface the top three epics where planned vs. delivered scope has drifted, and bring a one-page risk-and-bottleneck summary to product leadership within the first month — turning the existing tracking infrastructure into an actual decision-support tool rather than a status log.
positioning_narrative: Akshat shows up here as the execution-rigorous engineer-turned-PM who has already built the visibility and accountability infrastructure that this role is trying to maintain — specifically, he turned audit surfaces and delivery transparency into enterprise deal drivers at Hevo, not just internal process improvements. The strongest thread running through his background is discovering that operational opacity (untracked batch jobs, unclear incident ownership, reconciliation gaps) is itself a product problem with measurable business consequences, and fixing it with structured tooling and cross-functional discipline. The resume and cover letter should emphasize delivery tracking, cross-functional execution, and reporting clarity while de-emphasizing consumer marketplace and pricing stories that don't connect to institutional financial services or pipeline management.
